names.name: Bone Suckin' Sauce
names.said: Bone Suckin', with the g dropped on the label.

text.what: A Raleigh line of bottled sauces, of which the one that built the brand is Sweet Southern: cane sugar first, tomato puree second, water third, apple cider vinegar fourth, at six grams of sugar to the tablespoon. The house also bottles an Eastern Vinegar sauce, whose label puts apple cider vinegar and distilled vinegar first and tomato paste sixth, and a mustard whose seven ingredients name no tomato at all. One maker, three readings of the same state's shelf.
text.story:
The company dates the sauce to Raleigh in 1992 and calls the recipe a family one; the Sweet Southern page describes that bottle as the flavor the brand launched with. The mustard's page quotes Mr. Ford, of Ford's Foods, on making a sweet version of the house's sweet-and-spicy mustard without the heat.

The interesting part is on the backs of the bottles. Sweet Southern reads sugar, tomato, water, vinegar — the order of a Kansas City sauce, made in the eastern half of North Carolina, where the sauce a pit puts on a chopped hog has neither sugar nor tomato in it. The Eastern Vinegar bottle, sold alongside it, inverts that: two vinegars, then water, then cane sugar, with tomato paste down at six. The maker's own page for that bottle describes the tomato and molasses in it as a light hint behind the vinegar. *Inference —* a house that sells both is not choosing between the styles; it is selling the distance between them as two products.

recipes.title: Barbecue Sauce (Kansas City-style)
ingredients: 3 tablespoons (45 mL) finely minced yellow onion
4 teaspoons (20 mL) bottled liquid smoke flavor (hickory)
¼ teaspoon (1 mL) Louisiana-style red pepper sauce
recipes.text:
1. Combine all ingredients in a saucepan.
2. Mix well.
3. Simmer over low heat for 20 minutes, stirring occasionally.
recipes.note: A sugar-first tomato sauce of the same shape, freely licensed. The maker's own formula is not published; these are free-to-use recipes of the same family, for a cook who wants to make a jar.

recipes.title: Barbecue Sauce I
ingredients: 1 heaping tsp (6.66 mL) of ground coffee beans
A shot of whiskey or ½ shot of cognac
recipes.text:
1. Mix everything in a pot.
2. Let it simmer for around 30 minutes, stirring occasionally.

recipes.title: Sauce for Barbecues (receipt 335)
recipes.author: Mrs. A. P. Hill
recipes.text: Melt half a pound of butter; stir into it a large tablespoonful of mustard, half a teaspoonful of red pepper, one of black, salt to taste; add vinegar until the sauce has a strong acid taste. The quantity of vinegar will depend upon the strength of it. As soon as the meat becomes hot, begin to baste, and continue basting frequently until it is done; pour over the meat any sauce that remains.
recipes.note: The Southern mop of 1867 that pre-dates any tomato in a barbecue bottle.
